response.prediction: During a coronary artery bypass graft surgery, surgeons take several steps to prevent major blood loss. Before starting the operation, they carefully control the patient’s blood flow by using a heart-lung machine, which takes over the function of the heart and lungs and allows the surgeon to stop the heart temporarily. This makes it easier to work without a lot of bleeding. The surgeons also use special instruments and techniques to carefully clamp, or close off, the blood vessels they are working on, so blood does not flow out while they are connecting the new blood vessels. Additionally, they may give the patient medications to help the blood clot and sometimes use products that help the blood clot faster at the end of the surgery. These steps together help keep blood loss to a minimum during the procedure.
